{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABc74qvA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhGd_ls", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 227, "title": "Simplify extension Live: remove Input and output targets panel and show only actionable errors", "body": "## Goal

Make the extension **Live** screen focused on the actual experience: recording controls, graph-defined action buttons, Display output tabs, and errors that need user attention.

Implement **both** of the following agreed UX changes in this issue:

1. **Remove the "Input and output targets" panel from Live entirely.**
2. **Remove normal Node/runtime status messages from the visible Live surface. Only errors should appear as Node-related notifications.**

This is not a request to hide a handful of strings via regex; cleanly separate internal diagnostics from user-facing error notifications.

## 1. Remove Input and output targets

The current Live UI contains `<details id="targets"><summary>Input and output targets</summary>...` plus `#target-status`. `extension/target-controls.js` renders rows for `ChromeTabAudio`, `MicrophoneAudio`, `SelectedPageMediaAudio`, and `FocusedInputTextOutputNode`. This duplicates Graph Editor's responsibility and exposes implementation details in the primary Live UI.

**Required:**

- Remove the panel, heading, target rows, discovery button/select, and associated prominent `#target-status` surface from Live. Do not merely collapse it behind a details triangle.
- Remove or refactor the UI wiring that assumes the panel exists, including `TargetControls` DOM construction and rendering, `recorder.js` references, state handling and tests.
- **Keep Graph Editor responsible for which source/output Node types are connected.** `ChromeTabAudio` uses the invoking browser tab; microphone permissions remain managed by Start/browser permission flow; `FocusedInputTextOutputNode` retains its existing automatic focused-field behavior where supported. Removing a UI panel must not silently alter unrelated pipeline semantics.
- **`SelectedPageMediaAudio` currently requires selecting a specific page media element in this panel.** The user deliberately wants to defer designing a replacement: in a **future, separate task**, selection should happen on the target Web page itself. **Do not implement an on-page picker or any new replacement selector in this issue.**
- Handle that interim limitation explicitly: if `SelectedPageMediaAudio` needs a selection which is no longer possible in Live, do not silently record the wrong element, start in an invalid state, or leave Start mysteriously disabled. Show a concise actionable error identifying the source/limitation (and, if useful, instructing the user to choose `ChromeTabAudio` in Graph Editor for now). Other independent graph branches should not be broken unnecessarily. Document the temporary constraint.
- Remove stale state, inaccessible references, and dead UI controls; avoid unnecessary new settings or dialogs.

## 2. Node/runtime status: visible Live surface is errors only

At present, `extension/recorder.js`'s `renderNotices()` uses a **regular expression allowlist** to hide a few routine messages, and displays unfamiliar ones, such as:

```
textsummaryqwen35: Text Summary · Qwen3.5 2B: waiting for TEXT; model loads on first request.
```

This is a perfectly normal idle state, not a user-facing notification. Likewise, model loading, generation in progress, ready, completed, queue progress, etc. are not appropriate as ongoing messages in Live.

**Required:**

- Do not show **waiting / ready / loading / generating / processing / completion / normal progress** notifications from summary, translation, condition, Hold, speech, TTS, capture, etc. in the main Live interface. This applies regardless of which Node produces the message, including future Node types.
- Only **real errors requiring user attention** should be surfaced as Node-related notices in Live. Failures must remain clear and actionable, including model unavailable, permission errors, failed operation, and other relevant errors; avoid duplicated error lines and stale errors lingering into a new session.
- Do not classify messages by English text/regex (including special-casing `waiting for TEXT`). Prefer **structured event severity/status** at the source or a central normalization layer with explicit error handling, and route normal events away from the primary screen.
- Diagnostics can remain available through an **optional `Session details` area** (or equivalent troubleshooting view) without appearing in the main flow. Existing normal event data need not be discarded if it is useful for diagnostics.
- A minimal **overall session state** needed to understand Start/Stop/Cancel (e.g. recording/idle) can stay visible. Do not confuse that with displaying individual Node statuses. Graph Actions and Display output content remain visible and functional.
- Keep errors visible/accessibly announced, but do not reintroduce a permanent large status area for routine information.

## Technical touchpoints

- `extension/recorder.html` — remove `#targets`, `#target-status` and the old visible status notice area as appropriate
- `extension/recorder.js` — remove target-panel orchestration, `renderNotices` regex-based visible logging, route only actual errors to Live
- `extension/target-controls.js` — remove UI responsibility and preserve only non-UI target/session functions that remain necessary, if applicable
- `extension/session.js` — keep error and target state ownership consistent; no null DOM references
- `extension/graph.js`, `extension/graph-runtime.js` and Node event handlers as needed to distinguish error vs routine status
- Chrome extension/MV3/browser tests, docs and relevant manual test instructions

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Live view no longer contains an "Input and output targets" panel or its target rows, and it does not have an empty placeholder where the panel used to be.
- [ ] A graph with `ChromeTabAudio`, microphone or focused-field output continues using the existing invocation/permission behavior, with no additional target UI required.
- [ ] `SelectedPageMediaAudio` does not silently malfunction after removal of the old selector. Its temporary unavailability/selection limitation is explained via an actionable error when relevant. **On-page element selection is explicitly deferred.**
- [ ] The example `textsummaryqwen35: ... waiting for TEXT; model loads on first request` is absent from the normal Live view.
- [ ] Normal loading, inference, completion, idle and status/progress events from all Node categories **never appear** as user-facing Live messages; new Node messages do not accidentally leak through a regex fallback.
- [ ] Actual errors (model load/inference failure, missing resource, permission/selection errors, pipeline failures) remain accessible and clear in Live, without duplicate display or spurious success messages.
- [ ] Normal diagnostics can be inspected on demand, while Start/Stop/Cancel, Graph Actions, Display input tabs, copy-free reading panels and per-tab updates retain their behavior.
- [ ] Tests cover ordinary vs error events, stale error reset after restart, target-panel removal, selected-media transitional behavior and responsive/MV3 Live layout.
- [ ] Update help/documentation to match the simplified Live responsibilities and record tests actually executed.

## Scope

**Only remove the unwanted Live target panel and clean up visible Node status notifications.** Do not add a new Web-page picker, change Graph topology, or redesign the processing engine outside what's needed for correct error/status routing.", "url": "https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/227", "created_at": "2026-11-06T04:37:20Z", "state": "OPEN", "repository": "takahirox/my-audio-to-text", "labels": ["task"], "priority": null, "status": "In Progress", "is_archived": false}, "context": {}, "resources": {}, "allocation": {}, "instruction": null, "run_id": "61aff613e9f94eafac7df728dbf92f12"}
